newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says will retain EU veto.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says will retain EU veto.

text.p: Opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Tuesday that a Labour government would resist extension of qualified majority voting in the European Union. Brown told BBC radio Labour would not allow majority voting on immigration, foreign affairs, border controls or on taxation. "The British veto will remain on all these issues."
"We will pursue a policy of constructive engagement, participating in Europe so that we can get decisions that are made in the British national interest," Brown said.
"If we have to stand up to our partners and say they are wrong, we will."
Brown also said a Labour government would not stand by and allow the convergence criteria demanded of those wishing to sign up for a single European currency to be compromised.
"There can be no fudging of criteria," Brown told BBC radio. "The question about monetary union is not whether it can happen at a given point but whether it's sustainable."
